name: list_secrets
description: List the secrets of this org with each name, environmentVariable, description, and availability. Read each value through its environmentVariable. Needs only the workspace token. An active turn adds its session approvals to availability. Never returns values. Keep secret values out of output, files, and answers.

name: run_with_secrets
description: Run a shell command on this cloud computer with named secrets in its environment. Needs an active calling turn. Acts for the member whose message started that turn. Requests approval when needed and waits up to 90 seconds. A pending result ends without a command. After a late-answer notice, call again. Read each value through the environmentVariable from list_secrets. Two names that need one environment key fail before any request. Run those names separately. Returns filtered stdout, stderr, exitCode, and the environmentVariables name-to-variable map. Keep each value out of output, files, and answers. The filter hides only exact copies.

names.description: One or more secret names. A missing name asks a member for a temporary value.

command.description: Shell command to run with /bin/sh in this workspace. The request shows this text as the command you say you will run. Read values from the environment. Never put a value in this text.

reason.description: Why this command needs the named secrets.

name: run_mac_command
description: Ask to run a command on the active turn sender's connected Mac. Approval stays on that Mac.

name: create_workspace
description: Create a workspace with this workspace's owner and start its first message. Needs an active calling turn. Acts for the member whose message started that turn. Omitted model and effort use the owner's defaults. Fast mode requires explicit fast: true for a marked model. The reply gives the workspace number and link, and the first session link. These calls reach workspaces in this org. An omitted workspaceId names the calling workspace. Use names and returned links in normal answers. Workspace and session links show as chips. A session link holds both IDs. A Sent by: line names the sending session. Do not reply only to confirm it. Pass parentId to nest the new workspace. Nest work that belongs to the calling workspace's task: a part of a large task that can run in parallel, follow-up work that the task starts, work in another repository for the same task, or a change that needs its own pull request. Each separate pull request needs its own workspace. Omit parentId for unrelated work. When a member names the place, follow the member. Agents usually pass their own workspace ID from their instructions. The new workspace joins its parent's section, so sectionId has no effect with parentId. Nesting stops at depth 3. A create under a workspace at depth 3 fails with nesting_limit. Its message gives the parentId for a sibling. Start the sibling's name with a one-word group prefix, such as "Limits: ". The workspace in the reply gives parentId. The reply can give a notice about its section.

name.description: Optional workspace name. Use plain words separated by spaces. Avoid underscores unless the user tells you to add them. The app keeps the first line, without a final full stop, cut to 60 characters at a word.

firstSessionTitle.description: Optional first session title. Use plain words separated by spaces. Avoid underscores unless the user tells you to add them.

sectionId.description: A section ID from list_sections. Omission uses the default section. With parentId, the new workspace joins its parent's section.

requestId.description: Keep this ID to retry without another workspace, session, or message. Omission generates an ID.

fast.description: Use fast mode for a marked model. Creates default to false. Omission on send keeps the session speed.

parentId.description: Parent workspace ID. Agents usually pass their own workspace ID from their instructions. Omission makes a top-level workspace.

name: list_workspaces
description: List workspaces with their number, link, name, branch, state, and owner ID, login, and display name. Needs only the workspace token. Without filters or paging, returns every workspace, including archives. Use the actual message sender's member ID for their workspaces. Find another owner's ID in returned owner fields. Do not infer the owner from the token or active turn. These calls reach workspaces in this org. An omitted workspaceId names the calling workspace. Use names and returned links in normal answers. Workspace and session links show as chips. A session link holds both IDs. A Sent by: line names the sending session. Do not reply only to confirm it. Each entry gives parentId, or null for a top-level workspace. Pass parentId to list only the direct sub-workspaces of that workspace.

ownerId.description: A stable member ID from the actual message Sender line or workspace owner fields. A login is not an ID.

updatedSince.description: Signed safe-integer epoch timestamp in milliseconds. Select newer activity.

archived.description: Select archived workspaces with true, or other workspaces with false.

limit.description: Maximum entries. A limited reply gives hasMore. Omission returns every entry.

offset.description: Entries to skip before the next page.

parentId.description: Parent workspace ID. List only its direct sub-workspaces. An unknown ID gives an empty list.

name: get_workspace
description: Get workspace details, including owner, repository, base branch, section, activity, and restore times. Needs only the workspace token. These calls reach workspaces in this org. An omitted workspaceId names the calling workspace. Use names and returned links in normal answers. Workspace and session links show as chips. A session link holds both IDs. A Sent by: line names the sending session. Do not reply only to confirm it. The reply gives parentId, parent, depth, and children. The parent is a list entry or null. Children are direct sub-workspaces, oldest first, including archived ones.

workspaceId.description: A workspace ID from list_workspaces or a returned link. Defaults to the calling workspace.
